thread:
sam_support: FYI - Customer JenkinsHealth (acct jhealth) reports function-calling failures after today's model rollout. They see schema validation errors and some 401s for dedicated tokens. Latency also spiked. Need triage + rollback decision.

sam_support: Summary from the customer: 07:18 UTC first failed call, error: "tool_argument_missing: 'user_id'". They retried which multiplied billing and token counts.

sam_support: Example request they sent (redacted token):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-ded-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-model-3.0",
  "input": "Get user info",
  "functions": [
    {"name":"get_user","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"user_id":{"type":"string"}}}}
  ],
  "function_call": {"name":"get_user","arguments":{"user_id":"12345"}}
}
```

sam_support: Customer claims the model sometimes returned "function_call": {"name": "get_user", "arguments": "12345"} (arguments got coerced to string) or returned null and the service rejected it with schema validation.

anya_sre: Can you paste the request_id(s) and a few backend logs? Also which zone/dedicated pool was hit?

sam_support: Request IDs: req_9a7b1c, req_9a7b2d, req_9a7b5f. Hits show host pool: ded-us-west-1a-pool-3. Attaching the short trace snippet below.

sam_support: Trace(req_9a7b1c):
```
[07:19:02] ingress: auth ok for token sk-ded-REDACTED
[07:19:02] router: route -> ded-us-west-1a-pool-3 (model redwood-model-3.0)
[07:19:03] runtime: model response start
[07:19:03] runtime: emitted function_call name=get_user
[07:19:03] runtime: emitted arguments="12345" (raw bytes len=6)
[07:19:03] runtime: validation failed: expected object for arguments
[07:19:03] response: 400 schema_validation_error tool_argument_type_mismatch
```

kevin_ml: Thanks, digging in. We changed the function-arg serialization layer for v3.0 to prefer compact encoding for small payloads; looks like a bug where single-field objects get serialized as primitives in some quantized decoders. Repro on my local with same model binary.

kevin_ml: Repro snippet I used: `input-> model v3.0 -> emits function_call arguments as raw string when object has 1 property and property value is string`.

liz_custsuccess: Customer impact: they reported multiple failed requests and then retries, saw tokens billed for each attempt. They're asking for rollback and a note to their security/compliance team about the 401s. Also they lost a nightly job. Priority: P1 for their account.

max_product: What's the scope? Is this only for dedicated pools or hosted as well? Also any auth regression?

sam_support: So far repro is on dedicated pool ded-us-west-1a-pool-3 and a handful of hosted tenants hitting v3.0 variant. 401s appear in ~3 customers using rotated dedicated tokens — unclear if token validation is flakey or the client retried with expired token. Need SRE to look at auth logs correlated with the failed requests.

anya_sre: Checking auth logs now. I see some 401s around 07:19 for token verification failures: auth-service returned 401 for token lookup with backend error (db timeout). That seems separate but coincident. I'll open a pager if auth DB errors persist.

deploy-bot: rollout: model redwood-model-3.0 promoted 2026-03-17T06:12:00Z -> traffic 30% (us-west), 2026-03-17T07:05:00Z -> traffic 100% (us-west).

kevin_ml: Given immediate repro and a clear serialization regression for function args, recommend pausing/rolling back the v3.0 rollout in affected pools. We can hotfix the serializer, but rollback buys time.

anya_sre: Agree. Ops plan: rollback redwood-model-3.0 to prior stable v2.4 on ded-us-west-1a-pool-3 and reduce traffic for hosted region to 0% for v3.0. Who can approve rollback?

max_product: I approve emergency rollback for the affected pools. Need expected user impact and notice text.

kevin_ml: Hotfix ETA: ~3 hours to patch the serialization layer, test, and push a safe canary. Patch will ensure single-field objects remain objects.

liz_custsuccess: I'll draft an explanation and mitigation note for JenkinsHealth and offer credits for billing spikes. Can we get a confirmed rollback window?

anya_sre: Rolling back now (initiating). I'll post updates in 5m with status.

anya_sre: UPDATE: rollback triggered. Traffic for ded-us-west-1a-pool-3 moved back to redwood-model-2.4 at 07:34:22 UTC. Hosted region traffic for v3.0 reduced to 0% at 07:36:10 UTC.

sam_support: Customer confirms after rollback their job retried and then succeeded with v2.4. They reported reduced latency and no schema errors.

finance-bot: Observed billing event spike for acct jhealth between 07:18-07:30 UTC. Potential credit required - flagged to revenue ops.

kevin_ml: I'll cut a branch with the serializer fix and run internal fuzz tests across function-call shapes. After internal canary we can re-promote v3.0.

max_product: Plan for re-release: patch + controlled canary limited to non-dedicated hosted with monitoring alert for function-schema-mm mismatch rate. Approval required from eng-sre and product.

liz_custsuccess: I'll send an interim customer note: apology, brief root cause (model serializer bug caused malformed function args), rollback summary, and offer a billing credit.

sam_support: Thanks team. Action items: kevin - patch + tests; anya - monitor auth DB errors and confirm auth 401s are unrelated; max - coordinate canary policy; liz - customer comms + credit. I'll follow up after kevin's patch runs.

kevin_ml: one more datapoint: this bug only triggers when the model runs with quantized kernels on certain GPU drivers (us-west hosts). Adding driver constraints to canary to avoid regression surface.

anya_sre: noted. I'll also add a short alert rule: if function_schema_errors > 10/min in any pool, auto-scale down v3.0 to 0% traffic.

sam_support: closing loop with JenkinsHealth: they accepted credit offer and will allow us to test the patched model in a private canary before broad re-rollout.

max_product: good. mark as resolved for now but keep the incident tag until v3.0 is re-promoted and stable.
